title: Schedule Footnote: the Deductible a Benefit Calls For on Travel Protection Plans
content:
The deductible a benefit calls for, when a settlement is rated on a Travel Protection Plans certificate, turns on the benefit the insurer allowed and on whether the certificate has reached the plan's ceiling on deductibles withheld. The certificate has reached that ceiling when the deductibles already withheld from its settled payments in this policy term come to the plan's ceiling or more; what remains of the ceiling is the plan's ceiling less those deductibles, and the certificate has not reached the ceiling while what remains is above nothing.

Where the benefit allowed is the emergency medical benefit and the certificate has not reached the plan's ceiling on deductibles withheld, the deductible the benefit calls for is the deductible that benefit names.

Where the benefit allowed is any other benefit and the certificate has not reached the plan's ceiling on deductibles withheld, the deductible the benefit calls for is the plan's general deductible for each claim.

Where neither holds, the deductible the benefit calls for is nothing, 0.00 USD.

## The plan figures the three cases read

| Plan | Deductible the emergency medical benefit names, USD | General deductible for each claim, USD | Ceiling on deductibles withheld per policy, USD |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trip Basics Essential | 250.00 | 100.00 | 300.00 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 150.00 | 75.00 | 225.00 |
| TripGuard Plus | 100.00 | 50.00 | 150.00 |
| TripGuard Premier | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 100.00 | 50.00 | 150.00 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

## Reading the three cases

The first two cases are told apart by the benefit allowed alone: the emergency medical benefit takes the deductible that benefit names, and every other benefit takes the plan's general deductible for each claim. Both require that the certificate has not reached the plan's ceiling on deductibles withheld.

The third case is reached whenever the certificate has reached that ceiling, whatever the benefit allowed, and the deductible the benefit calls for is then 0.00 USD.

Hypothetically, on a plan whose ceiling is 150.00 USD and whose general deductible is 50.00 USD, a certificate from which 100.00 USD has already been withheld in this policy term has 50.00 USD remaining of the ceiling, which is above nothing, so it has not reached the ceiling and the deductible the benefit calls for is 50.00 USD on a benefit other than emergency medical. Had 150.00 USD already been withheld, nothing would remain of the ceiling, the certificate would have reached it, and the deductible the benefit calls for would be 0.00 USD.
